description: Small beetles used as biological control insects against Euphorbia esula (Leaf Spurge). The larvae feed on the roots while the adults consume the leaves, reducing the plant's growth and reproduction.
symptoms: Weakened or dying plants over time
favorable_conditions: Well-drained soils that favor larval development
spread: Human introduction for biological control programs
management: Use as a biological control agent
Avoid pesticides that can kill Aphthona populations
chemical_control: Not applicable: used as a biological control agent
prevention: Maintain healthy beetle populations for sustainable control
source: USDA Leaf Spurge Biological Control Program

description: A caterpillar that mainly attacks the stems and roots of maize, sorghum, and other grasses, causing wilting and death of young seedlings.
symptoms: Wilting and yellowing of young plants
Holes and tunnels at the base of stems
favorable_conditions: Hot and dry climates that favor egg laying
spread: Eggs laid in the soil or at the base of plants
Larvae move to attack young stems
Movement of infested plants or plant material
management: Deep planting to protect young seedlings
chemical_control: Systemic or soil-applied insecticides (e.g., Chlorpyrifos, Imidacloprid)
prevention: Keep fields free of plant debris
Monitor young plants and treat early if infestation appears
